stories.title: College Football fans are missing their villains
stories.summary: Everyone wanted parity, but now that we have it, there is nobody left to hate. As a result the sport no longer has a true villain to hate, and petty hate watching is the backbone of college football fanaticism. For the better part of two decades, Nick Saban was the sport's lightning rod, his Crimson Tide the designated villain. With life changing money not yet a part of the equation for student athletes, Saban was able to sell his development program to stack the two deep with NFL talent. Alabama routinely redshirted players that could have started immediately at 50 programs across the country, and that depth resulted in a dynasty that every other fanbase united against.

stories.title: Jenson Button delivers stinging verdict on Esteban Ocon's F1 career following Haas bust up
stories.summary: Jenson Button reckons Esteban Ocon may have "possibly thrown away the rest of his career in F1" after Haas stood him down at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Haas replaced Ocon with reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa before Saturday's final practice and still has not said why. Button reacted to Ocon's statement on Sky Sports F1. The former world champion started by pointing to the pressure a driver is under once his team has moved on. "It's always difficult for a driver when you are out and your team are looking at someone else," he said. He had little sympathy for how Ocon handled it, though, and added that the 22 drivers on the grid are among the best in the world.
